key_insight: Large language models can act as meta-designers by writing human-readable code that encodes general design rules, enabling generation of entire families of quantum experiments that are both interpretable and scalable.
problem_solved: Exploration and generation of quantum experiment designs is slow, manual, and hard to scale or interpret; this approach automates design rule creation and produces reproducible, extensible experiment families.
method: Prompt and fine-tune LMs to output human-readable code/templates that capture high-level quantum design rules (meta-design).
Use those templates programmatically to generate many concrete experiment variants and evaluate them via simulation or experimental constraints.
Iteratively refine templates with feedback from evaluations to improve performance, interpretability, and scalability of discovered designs.
impact: Enables AI practitioners to use LMs as interpretable design engines for physical science discovery, accelerating search over large design spaces and producing reusable design rules for downstream experiments.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: LM → human-readable code/templates → generated experiment families → simulation/validation loop.
Side-by-side code snippet (readable template) and the corresponding experimental schematic it produces.
Heatmap or scatter plot showing design-space coverage and performance improvement over iterations.
Icon set: language model, code file, lab apparatus (optics/quantum), and a growth/scale arrow to show scalability.
paper_title: Meta-designing quantum experiments with language models
paper_authors: Sören Arlt, Haonan Duan, Felix Li, Sang Michael Xie, Yuhuai Wu
